candidates.name: Science and Industry Museum
candidates.price: Free, except for temporary exhibits (prices vary)
candidates.content: This is a great museum for those interested in technology and industrial heritage: sited at one end of the world's first passenger railway line. The working cotton weaving machines are particularly worth experiencing. Catch one of

candidates.name: Manchester Jewish Museum
candidates.hours: Sun-Thu 10:00-16:00, Fri 10:00-13:00, closed Sat & Jewish holidays
candidates.content: Manchester has Britain's largest Jewish population outside London; this museum tells their story. From being barely tolerated in the 18th C, they prospered in the 19th C (as did the entire city) in textiles and tailoring, and move

candidates.name: The Portico Library and Gallery
candidates.content: The Portico has been an exclusive members-only library since the early 19th century and many of Manchester's luminaries have been patrons of the Portico over the years. Now hosting its own public gallery and providing admission to

candidates.name: St. Mary's (The Hidden Gem)
candidates.hours: Mon-Thu Fri 9:30AM-4PM, Sat 9:30AM-6PM, Sun 10AM-2PM (services Mon-Fri 12:30PM, Sat noon and 5:15PM, Sun 8:30AM and 1:30PM)
candidates.content: This little traditional Catholic church dates from 1794, making it the oldest purpose-built post-Reformation Catholic church in England. It is an active church, with the largest congregation of any of the city-centre churches in M

candidates.name: People's History Museum
candidates.content: This little museum down by the river on the border of Manchester and Salford aims to document the way the lives of ordinary people have developed since the industrial revolution. The museum owns many artifacts and documentation fr

candidates.name: Imperial War Museum North
candidates.content: While the IWM in London contains tanks, guns, planes and uniforms, the North museum is focused on the social impacts of war, with less military hardware on display.

candidates.name: The Lowry
candidates.content: This award-winning modern building contains two theatres and a large art gallery, with many works by L.S. Lowry (1887-1976). When he was 22 his family moved from a leafy suburb to Pendlebury, an industrial district of Salford; he

candidates.name: Whitworth Art Gallery
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 10AM-5PM, Sun 2-5PM. Closed Good Fri and Christmas to New Year
candidates.content: Manchester University's art gallery combines more modern art than the Manchester Art Gallery with displays of watercolors, prints, textiles and wallpapers.

candidates.name: Chetham's School of Music & Library
candidates.content: Library M-F 9AM-12:30PM, 1:30-4:30PM, closed Bank Holidays, call in advance; School is closed to general public. Chetham's is an independent private school of music and public library housed in the medieval priests' college next t

candidates.name: Manchester Art Gallery
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10AM-5PM and bank holidays except Christmas, New Year, and Good Fri
candidates.content: The principal wing is the work of Sir Charles Barry, also architect of the House of Parliament. Manchester's central art gallery is home to a huge collection of 19th-century and earlier works, including paintings by Canaletto, Con

candidates.name: St. Ann's Church
candidates.hours: closed Mon, Tue-Fri 11AM-5PM, Sat 11AM-6PM, Sun 8:30AM-6PM. see website for service times.
candidates.content: Daily daytime, check the website for service times. St. Ann's Church is the main parish church of Manchester and one of only two surviving Medieval churches in the city centre (the other is the cathedral). It is also a venue for m

candidates.name: Royal Exchange
candidates.price: Free entry to theatre building, theatre tickets vary
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 9:30AM-late (depending on length of evening's performance)
candidates.content: The neo-classical Royal Exchange was the commercial heart of Manchester's and therefore the world's cotton trade. The main trading hall, essentially a neo-Roman basilica, was at one time the largest commercial room in the world. I

candidates.name: St. John's Gardens
candidates.content: The site of the former St. John's Church has become central Manchester's most beautiful park. Come here in the summer to see the flowers and bring some bread for the hundreds of birds that make St. John's their home.

candidates.name: Roman Fort
candidates.content: Not much survives of Manchester's four Roman settlements, but what is left can be seen in the gardens of Castlefield running from Liverpool Road down to Castle Street. The North Gate of the fourth fort on Duke Street, along with a

candidates.name: Museum of Transport
candidates.content: Large collection of old buses & similar memorabilia in a former depot.

candidates.name: Manchester Museum
candidates.content: Manchester University's own museum is like a mini version of London's Natural History Museum and boasts real dinosaur skeletons (including Stan the T-Rex), Egyptian mummies, and architect Alfred Waterhouse's huge taxidermy collect

candidates.name: Manchester Cathedral
candidates.content: Cathedral Yard (Visitor Centre at 10 Cateaton Street, around the corner). Cathedral M-F 8AM-7PM, Sa 8AM-5PM, Su 8:30AM-7:30PM, check website for service times and events; Visitor Centre is open M-Sa 10AM-4:30PM, Su 11:30AM-4PM. On

candidates.name: Manchester Central
candidates.content: Manchester Central (formerly "G-MEX") was once Manchester Central railway station and it carries the air of many of the grand stations in London with its enormous arched steel frame and giant railway clock. These days it is home t

candidates.name: Bridgewater Hall
candidates.content: Manchester's main classical music venue is a stunning musically-inspired building dating from 1996. It is home to the world-famous Hallé orchestra and boasts an enormous 5500-pipe organ across the whole of one wall. The building i

candidates.name: Central Library
candidates.hours: Department opening hours vary, see web site
candidates.content: You can't miss this striking circular neo-Classical building when passing through St. Peter's Square. Following a major renovation completed in 2014, Central Library is well worth visit, if not for its vast selection of resources

candidates.name: John Rylands Library
candidates.content: After closing for refurbishment, the John Rylands Library is now open to the public. It now has access to all floors and a new entrance and cafe to the side of the building on Spinningfields. The John Rylands library is a beautifu

candidates.name: Manchester Opera House
candidates.content: Sister theatre to The Palace Theatre. Host to touring musicals, ballet, concerts.

candidates.name: Centre for Chinese Contemporary Art
candidates.content: Small, alternative Chinese art gallery. Closed until 2023

candidates.name: Heaton Park
candidates.content: Manchester's largest open space and one of the largest municipal parks in Europe. The park is home to a former stately home, vintage trams (run Apr-Oct Sa Su) and golf course.

candidates.name: Sackville Gardens
candidates.content: This small park in the heart of The Village is notable for its memorial to Alan Turing, the father of modern computer science, whose homosexuality in an age of intolerance led to his suicide. The bronze statue on a park bench bear

candidates.name: Manchester Town Hall
candidates.content: This imposing and beautiful neo-Gothic masterpiece by Alfred Waterhouse is the official headquarters of the Manchester City Council, but its job is largely ceremonial now. Most of the offices have moved to the more practical exten

candidates.name: The Albert Hall
candidates.content: An ornate former Wesleyan chapel that has been converted into a music venue, bar and restaurant. The hall plays host to a number of exciting acts on a regular basis. For specific information, see the venue's website.

candidates.name: The Curry Mile
candidates.content: A one mile long, neon light illuminated, stretch of Wilmslow Road with wall to wall curry houses, kebab shops, sari shops, and jewellery stores. The best curry in Manchester can be had here, but the community is an attraction in i

candidates.name: FC United of Manchester
candidates.price: Match tickets adult £12, concs £7, U18s £3, pay on the gate
candidates.content: This breakaway club was formed in 2005 by Man United supporters alienated by Malcolm Glazer's takeover, and it continues to be entirely supporter-owned. They play in Northern Premier League, the seventh tier of English football. T

candidates.name: Sportcity
candidates.content: This big complex was developed for the 2002 Commonwealth Games. Its main components are Manchester City football stadium (now the Etihad), the Regional Athletics Arena, the National Squash Centre, and the National Cycling Centre w

candidates.name: Manchester City FC
candidates.content: City play soccer in the Premier League, England's top tier, and since 2013 have overtaken old rivals Man United. Their home ground is Etihad Stadium, capacity 55,000. It has a museum and a stadium tour, adults £7, conc £4.50, hour

candidates.name: Manchester Pride festival
candidates.content: The Village hosts a major pride festival every year when the whole region of town is closed to the public for an expensive and exclusive weekend for gay and gay-friendly people from all over the UK.

candidates.name: Manchester United FC
candidates.content: United plays soccer in the Premier League, England's top tier. The stadium has a capacity of 75,000, and sells out against top-calibre opposition, such as the other big names in English football (especially Liverpool and Leeds Uni

candidates.name: Lancashire CCC
candidates.content: Lancashire CCC were relegated in 2024 and now play in Division Two of the County Championship. Test matches (5-day internationals) are also played here. Also here are Manchester Originals men's and women's teams playing in The Hun

candidates.name: HOME
candidates.content: Manchester's contemporary arts and film centre with five cinema screens & two theatres. Daily showings of independent & foreign language films and gallery space. The centre also houses a cafe-bar and a restaurant. Film prices are

candidates.name: The Palace Theatre
candidates.content: Hosts major touring shows.

candidates.name: The Printworks
candidates.content: Attraction opening times vary. Originally the home of Manchester's newspaper offices, the Printworks is now a covered street where it's night time all day long. It is the home of several well-known restaurants including Hard Rock

candidates.name: Piccadilly Gardens
candidates.content: Relax and watch the world go by in Piccadilly Gardens - the lung at the centre of the city. The Gardens are also home to the controversial concrete 'Berlin Wall', which houses cafés and seating.

candidates.name: National Cycling Centre
candidates.content: Britain's first indoor Olympic cycling track; a great place to try out the sport and to see the self-proclaimed 'home of British cycling'. Check website for times as the track is often booked out for Team GB training.

candidates.name: Chinese New Year
candidates.content: Follows a lunar calendar, so the next is Saturday, 10 February 2024, starting the Year of the Dragon. Expect firecrackers, drums and weaving dragons around Chinatown.

candidates.name: Manchester United Museum & Tour
candidates.content: Tour of the stadium facilities, plus museum of the club's history from its 1878 founding as Newton Heath, through the managerial eras of Busby and Ferguson, and a glittering cast of players. Exit via the gift shop: the club mercha

candidates.name: Manchester Arena
candidates.content: The largest indoor arena in Europe (21,000 capacity) hosts most of the world's most famous music and comedy acts, plus theatre and international boxing.

candidates.name: Infinity
candidates.content: A wellness club just outside the city centre. The main entrance is in the back of the building. Very friendly staff and modern infrastructure.

candidates.name: MediaCityUK
candidates.content: Has TV studios that you can visit.

candidates.name: Chill Factore
candidates.content: Ski on a 180-m artificial snow slope for skiing and snowboarding.

candidates.name: iFLY
candidates.content: Not quite skydiving, as you float in a wind tunnel with no parachutes involved.

candidates.name: Manchester Aquatics Centre
candidates.content: Swim at the Aquatic Centre.

candidates.name: Stoller Hall
candidates.content: Concert Hall associated with Chetham's School of Music. Predominantly Music; Classical, Folk, Jazz

candidates.name: Joseph Holt Brewery
candidates.content: Beers on sale and managed pubs throughout the city.

candidates.name: The Marble Arch Inn
candidates.content: Real ale brewed by their own brewery Marble and cask ale from micro-breweries nationwide.

candidates.name: Dukes 92
candidates.content: By far the most popular venue in Castlefield, Dukes 92 has an unusual, but successful, mix of antique furniture, modern deep leather sofas, and minimalist décor. Although relatively quiet in winter, it is hugely popular on hot sum

candidates.name: Oxnoble
candidates.content: Away from the Castlefield basin on Liverpool Road you will find The Oxnoble. It has the distinction of being the only pub in the country to be named after a potato - the Ox Noble.

candidates.name: White Lion
candidates.content: Modernised traditional pub, although it does feature on its walls an interesting aerial photograph of pre-developed Castlefield. Soundtrack of soul and funk with congenial staff set it apart from the others.

candidates.name: Bulls Head
candidates.content: Traditional pub with Victorian exterior, diagonally opposite rear entrance of Piccadilly station. Lunchtime food on weekdays. May close early if empty.

candidates.name: Sofa
candidates.content: Nice bar, with (surprisingly!) sofas and wooden floors. DJs on the weekends, also sells tickets to some of the bigger club nights in town.

candidates.name: Marble Arch Inn
candidates.hours: Sun-Tue noon-10PM, Wed Thu noon-11PM, Fri Sat noon-midnight; food: Sun noon-7PM, Mon-Thu noon-8PM, Fri Sat noon-9PM
candidates.content: Spectacular Victorian show-pub with beer from local Marble brewery. Inside, the pub has a high, glazed ceiling, ceramic walls and a bar that slopes down with the hill. Great beer & food makes the walk here worthwhile.

candidates.name: Matt and Phreds
candidates.content: Good little tucked away jazz club. Also serves up good pizza. They have jazz bands every night except Mondays (when it's closed) at 10PM. There is free entry before 8PM. If you want to enjoy the jazz seated, seats have to be booke

candidates.name: Britons Protection
candidates.content: Behind the stage door entrance of the Bridgewater Hall. It is here where many a poor mug "took The King's Shilling" and found himself press-ganged into the army. Largest selection of whisky in the city.

candidates.name: Society
candidates.content: Bar run by the Vocation brewery featuring a large choice of craft beers with a shared food space. Also Cocktail & wine bar. Coffee is available.

candidates.name: Peveril of the Peak
candidates.hours: Mon-Thu noon-11PM, Fri Sat noon-midnight, Sun noon-10:30PM
candidates.content: Spectacular green tiled exterior and traditional room layout form this very traditional pub. Real Ales available.

candidates.name: Molly House
candidates.hours: Sun-Tue noon-midnight, Wed Thu noon-1AM, Fri Sat noon-2AM. Food: noon-8PM
candidates.content: Bar & cafe with a good reputation for food.

candidates.name: The Metropolitan
candidates.content: Pub - serves both food and drink.

candidates.name: Samsi
candidates.content: City centre. A great sushi restaurant that also caters well for those that don't like raw fish. With a well-stocked, but small Japanese supermarket below (accessed from inside the restaurant).

candidates.name: Desi Roots
candidates.content: Traditional Indian Restaurant

candidates.name: The Angel Pub
candidates.content: A traditional English pub just off the Rochdale road, Manchester city centre. The pub serves real ales, fine wines and highly acclaimed food prepared by award winning celebrity chef Robert Owen Brown.

candidates.name: Mackie Mayor
candidates.content: Food Court in 1858 Grade II listed former market building. 6 independent kitchens and also bars. Beers from Manchester's Blackjack brewery. Tables are shared and are not bookable.

candidates.name: Deansgate Food Bar & Grill
candidates.content: Situated next to Deansgate station, it's a cheap and friendly authentic greasy spoon.

candidates.name: Number 1's
candidates.content: A really cheap Chinese buffet.

candidates.name: Tokyo Season
candidates.content: Serves traditional Japanese dishes at reasonable prices, with a full menu of drinks also available including Asian and world beers, spirits and wines.

candidates.name: ZOUK
candidates.content: Indian restaurant specialized in traditional south Asian cuisine and finger food.

candidates.name: Wing's Dai Pai Dong
candidates.content: Set around a sushi counter, this eatery serves a variety of mainstream Cantonese (Hong Kong), Thai, and Japanese dishes. The Hong Kong style roasting dishes are particularly good value and well-made. Typically any mixture of Char

candidates.name: Dimitri's
candidates.content: A taverna with live acts as well as underground seating in a plush environment. Food and drink is competitively priced but well worth the money for the spectacular quality and authenticity of the food and dining experience as a wh

candidates.name: Tepanyaki
candidates.content: Impressive and expensive tepanyaki restaurant. Really good food, but pricey.

candidates.name: Tropeiro
candidates.content: True Brazilian barbeque that serves eleven cuts of meat from chicken, pork, lamb and beef and a range of salads and side-dishes. Also tasty caiprinha cocktails.

december.text: There are many theatres and concert venues in Manchester: The Opera House, Palace Theatre, Royal Exchange, HOME (Arts Centre), Dancehouse Theatre, The Contact, and The Lowry at The Quays (which has three theatre spaces). Further afield, The Bolton Octagon, Bury Met, Oldham Coliseum, the lovingly restored 1930s Stockpor

Every Christmas time, continental style Christmas markets take place in Albert Square, in St. Ann's Square, and along both New Cathedral Street and Brazennose Street. You can buy all the usual Continental and British Christmas curios as well as various foodstuffs. Good fun and very atmospheric at night when it's all li

Also at Christmas, into the new year, there are open air skating rinks in Spinningfields as well as a snow slide and other attractions at Piccadilly Gardens. There is also a winterbar at the Spinningfields location.

Also upmarket is a new venture by the side of the Museum of Science and Industry. This is Akbar's on Liverpool Road and they claim, on the side of buses, to be "probably the best Indian restaurant in the North of England". Also popular in town are the two EastZEast; the original is under the Ibis Hotel, behind the form

During the period leading up to Christmas from November, there is a Christmas Market stretching from the Town Hall towards St Ann's Square and New Cathedral Street. Chinese New Year: Follows a lunar calendar, so the next is Saturday, 10 February 2024, starting the Year of the Dragon. Expect firecrackers, drums and weaving dragons around Chinatown.

From late November to Christmas, a large Christmas market sets up in Albert Square and on the streets leading up to it. The market runs from 16 Nov - 20 Dec and is open everyday from 10AM to 8PM.
